title: Principals, trust domains, protected assets and credential requirements

statuses.planned: Defined by accepted authority (blueprint, plan, decision or contract) but not built or not enforced yet. Needs sources.
statuses.observed: Exists today and is shown by committed evidence. Needs evidence links.
statuses.unknown: Not established from the accepted records or the committed evidence. Needs a finding.
statuses.conflict: Two accepted records disagree. Needs a finding.

authority_classes.owner: The Owner's own authority: approval, protected merge, policy and governance change, publication, privileged host change.
authority_classes.admin: System administration of a component: Gitea site administration, guest root equivalence (Moby group), Windows Administrators.
authority_classes.executor: The privileged effect executor's authority over allowlisted external effects and the effect receipts.
authority_classes.management: Management of execution: the Agent Server management API, the guest operator login, CI runner registration.
authority_classes.scoped: A least-privilege role credential limited to one role's own resources (a bot's repository writes, one conversation's inner server).
authority_classes.guest-local: A secret that exists only inside one execution guest for its own services.
authority_classes.provider: Access to an external model or service provider account.

trust_domains.name: Owner
trust_domains.description: The Owner's identity and decisions, protected policy and the Owner's host account. Same-account shell access can defeat an otherwise sound approval design.

trust_domains.name: Trusted management
trust_domains.description: The minimal dispatch broker or restricted launcher, the Integration Service, the authorization verifier and the inference broker, on the trusted control side and never mounted into agent execution.

trust_domains.name: Privileged effect
trust_domains.description: The restricted operation executor and its effect receipts, behind a separate OS credential boundary.

trust_domains.name: Git hosting
trust_domains.description: The Gitea server, its host and its site administration. Gitea's protections do not survive compromise of its administrator or host.

trust_domains.name: Execution guest control
trust_domains.description: The managed Linux execution VM's own system: guest root, the outer Agent Server's service user and the guest's own Moby. The VM is a host-protection boundary; this domain holds the guest's Docker authority and must stay unreachable from untrusted engineering.

trust_domains.name: Untrusted engineering
trust_domains.description: Planner and builder agents, the ACP provider process and build or test workloads, each in a per-conversation container inside the guest. Assumed hostile.

trust_domains.name: Review
trust_domains.description: Independent reviewer attempts: a separate session, runner or model and context from the builder; may review, never merge.

trust_domains.name: Untrusted CI
trust_domains.description: CI jobs that execute pull-request code: no Owner, release or signing secret, no host Docker socket.

trust_domains.name: CI runner host
trust_domains.description: A dedicated, disposable CI guest of the strong tier (a CI variant of the QEMU profile; never the Owner host or the execution guest) whose runner service registers with Gitea and launches disposable job containers; its only path off the guest is the ci-control forward to Gitea's runner RPC, an Owner act (decision 0016 (Proposed)).

identity.planned: A separate Gitea Owner account, the only identity on the authorization branch's merge allowlist; privileged host acts by the Owner's interactive UAC approval of a specifically authorized operation.
identity.observed: The Owner directs the work through the Overseer; Owner decisions and authorizations are recorded in decisions/ and evidence/bootstrap-log.md; host acts A1 and A3 were approved by interactive UAC consent. No authenticated Owner authorization record exists yet.

identity.planned: The Owner's own interactive account. It holds no executor or service identity, and no executor credential is stored in its Credential Manager.
identity.observed: Medium-integrity token, Administrators deny-only, no SeTakeOwnership/SeBackup/SeRestore, UAC on with secure-desktop consent. It runs QEMU as an ordinary user process (no service, no elevation) and owns the guest-state root, whose ACL holds only this account, SYSTEM and Administrators.

identity.planned: No independent identity is planned for them. Engineering work moves into the guest (td-untrusted-engineering) and privileged work to separate identities (the management service and the executor at G-04.2.1).
identity.observed: Claude Code sessions (Overseer, Architect, Builder) running as the Owner's Windows account. They are not independently isolated security principals; their elevation is gated only by the Owner's interactive UAC consent, which is not an OS security boundary, and they hold no standing elevation.

principals.name: Trusted dispatcher and restricted launcher

identity.planned: The trusted dispatcher identity and network admitted to the Agent Server's create and admin routes (S-01.3.1). It alone holds the Agent Server session key and, through the Agent Server, Docker authority; it checks accepted Work, policy revision, mounts, network and resource budget before it starts a conversation.

principals.notes: Today its role is performed by the Owner's account through tools/guest.py over the management SSH channel (F-04.2).

identity.planned: One lightweight local process for ordinary adapters, with its own identity; custody of integration.sqlite moves to it. It cannot write effect receipts.
A small read-only verifier: a webhook only wakes it; it reads the protected ref, the PR, merged_by, the exact blob and the policy, and never executes.
identity.observed: Only its Gitea identity exists (S-01.2.2): aieh-bot-verifier, a restricted, non-administrator Gitea Bot account without a password, read collaborator of the fixture, with a token of scope read:repository only in the Owner account's Credential Manager. It read the protected branch, a PR with merged_by and a blob; every write was refused by scope. No verifier is built.

principals.name: Owner authorization recorder

identity.planned: A deterministic, non-model recorder, the sole custodian of cred-gitea-owner-account (decision 0012, Proposed). On a recorded Owner decision it merges one exact operation manifest into the protected authorization branch as aieh-owner: HTTP basic authentication with the password read from the credential provider into memory for each command; never a token, sudo, force_merge or auto-merge; merge commits only, with head_commit_id and the decision trailers; a write-ahead receipt in the integration store. It has no agent-callable or MCP surface and runs only in the main session on an Owner decision.

principals.notes: Built at P-04.2 (integrations/owner/authorization_recorder.py, task owner:authorize) and exercised against a fake Gitea only; it has merged nothing on a real Gitea. During bootstrap it runs as a process of the Owner's Windows account, which the host-side bootstrap agents share (fd-bootstrap-shared-identity; decision 0010).

identity.planned: The host-side broker behind the guest's `inference` endpoint class: the only path to provider credentials, which never enter the guest.

principals.name: Privileged effect executor

identity.planned: A genuinely separate Windows identity created by Owner act A4 at G-04.2.1, preferably a service identity such as a virtual service account; Modify on the effects root only; it applies only typed, allowlisted effects.

principals.notes: Nothing live exists: no effects root, executor principal, service or scheduled task (decision 0004, Current facts).

identity.planned: Named only as a separately credentialed environment that runs narrowly authorized release or deployment jobs after verifying the protected revision.
The Gitea instance's site administrator. Can change protection rules and impersonate users, so it is in the trusted computing base and is never exposed to agents or CI.
identity.observed: aieh-site-admin, created by F-06.1 with Gitea's CLI as the instance's administrator account. Its password is harness-held: task gitea:finalize-credentials (Owner directive of 2026-11-07, no Owner sign-in) set it through Gitea's forced change and revoked the account's three leftover tokens (S-01.2.2). Gitea administration during bootstrap is performed by the Owner's host account (observed performer owner-os-account): identities, bots and tokens through Gitea's CLI, which needs no password; the S-01.2.2 fixture through the API as the site administrator, by basic authentication with the password in memory. Its merge and force-merge of a proposal PR were refused (405) by branch protection with the merge override blocked.

identity.planned: A per-conversation container started by the guest's Agent Server Docker runtime: approved read-only definitions, a working copy only, a minimal tool set; a dedicated Gitea 28 token-only bot account with non-admin repository write and PR scope. No Owner, merge, admin, executor, Docker or guest-management credential.
identity.observed: Only the container identity is observed, for the no-LLM fixture conversation: uid:gid of the Agent Server's service user (999:989), cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, exactly three binds under the server's scratch, port 8000 published on the guest's loopback only, and its own per-conversation OH_SECRET_KEY and session key in its environment. No agent workload, LLM or repository content has run. Its Gitea identities exist (S-01.2.2): aieh-bot-planner and aieh-bot-builder, non-administrator Gitea Bot accounts without passwords, each with a token of scope write:repository only in the Owner account's Credential Manager pending the dispatcher; no agent has held either. S-01.3.2 proved its job environment from inside two disposable conversation containers: no engine socket or engine API, no route of the outer Agent Server at any address, no host service through SLIRP's 10.0.2.2, and no fingerprint of the outer session key, OH_SECRET_KEY or any Gitea bot token in its readable files or process environments; root is not obtainable (no_new_privs).

identity.planned: A separate session, runner or model and context from the builder; its own Gitea bot identity that can submit reviews but cannot merge, administer or reach the executor.
identity.observed: Only its Gitea identity exists (S-01.2.2): aieh-bot-reviewer, a restricted, non-administrator Gitea Bot account without a password, read collaborator of the fixture, with a token of scope write:repository in the Owner account's Credential Manager (Gitea 28.3.0 needs write:repository to submit a review). It reviewed; its pushes, merges and settings changes were refused; it can open a PR (fd-gitea-reader-opens-pr). No reviewer session has run. Its runs are to execute in the same per-conversation job environment, proved at S-01.3.2 without a reviewer session.

identity.planned: A disposable container or VM on the dedicated runner host, with a restricted Gitea job token; no host-mode execution, broad container socket, user home or Owner credential. The runner containment profile (Q-02.2.1, proved by Q-02.2.2 and Q-02.3.2) carries the job constraints S-01.3.2 established for the conversation containers: no engine socket or engine TCP endpoint; no management key, Owner, admin or bot token; no privileged mode; no host-path mount beyond the scoped workspace (declared in provisioning.agent_server.jobs.ci, not verified: no CI runner exists).

act_runner (pinned at Q-02.2.1) in a dedicated disposable CI guest, as a dedicated guest service user in that guest's docker group (root-equivalent inside the CI guest only). It registers once to the governance repository with a registration token delivered in memory and reset before and after, then holds only its persistent runner token, root-owned outside every mount and unreachable from the job filesystem. It polls Gitea's runner RPC over the ci-control forward and launches each job as a disposable container (decision 0016 (Proposed)).
Root inside the execution guest, reached only through cloud-init at create and declared systemd units.
identity.observed: Root SSH login is refused (PermitRootLogin no). Root acts only in the single-use provision step (triggered once by a host marker, consuming only seed-pinned sha256 values) and in two read-only facts reporters (at boot, and on demand at most 20 runs in 60 s).

identity.planned: The guest's own service principal for the Agent Server: a system user with no login, in group docker, reaching only the guest's own daemon socket.
identity.observed: System user openhands (uid 999), shell nologin, password locked, groups openhands and docker; runs aieh-agent-server.service with NoNewPrivileges, an empty capability set, ProtectSystem=strict and IPAddressDeny=any except localhost; its process environment is readable only by itself and root.

identity.planned: The guest's non-root login for operators and provisioning: exec is never offered to agents, who reach the guest only through the Agent Server path.
identity.observed: User agent (uid 1000), no sudo, not in group docker (connect to both daemon sockets: EACCES). SSH login only with the per-instance key over the host-loopback forward. Host tooling uses it for exec, exchange, the provisioning upload, the facts requests and the API probes, and it can read the Agent Server session key (root:agent 0440). During bootstrap it is the dispatcher's interim vantage (the Owner's account through tools/guest.py); no agent workload has the login or its key (S-01.3.1).

credentials.name: The Owner's interactive UAC consent
credentials.storage: Not stored: an interactive secure-desktop approval of one specifically authorized elevated operation that an agent may initiate.
credentials.scope: One elevated host operation (A1, A3, A4 and effects-store restore).
credentials.lifetime: One operation.
credentials.notes: Consent, not a boundary: UAC is not an OS security boundary between processes of the Owner's account (decision 0004, clarification 5).

credentials.name: The Owner's push credential for the public GitHub repository
credentials.storage: The Owner's host credential store or key (not inspected).
credentials.scope: Push to the public repository; publication.
credentials.lifetime: Unknown.

credentials.name: The Owner's coding-assistant login used by the host-side agent sessions
credentials.storage: The coding assistant's own login storage in the Owner's account (not inspected).
credentials.scope: Model access under the Owner's provider account; it grants no approval, merge, policy or privileged host authority in this system.
credentials.lifetime: Unknown.

credentials.name: Per-instance SSH key for the guest operator login
credentials.storage: The per-instance directory under the guest-state root (ACL: the Owner's account, SYSTEM, Administrators); never ~/.ssh. Generated at create with the system ssh-keygen.
credentials.scope: SSH and SFTP as guest user agent over the host-loopback forward: exec, exchange, provisioning upload and session-key export.
credentials.lifetime: The instance: destroy removes it; recreate issues a new one.

credentials.name: Guest SSH host keys
credentials.storage: Inside the guest; the fingerprints reach the host from cloud-init's serial-log block into the instance's known_hosts.
credentials.scope: Host authentication of the guest's sshd.
credentials.lifetime: Regenerated at every create.

credentials.name: Agent Server session API key (OH_SESSION_API_KEYS_0)
credentials.storage: Generated in the guest by the root step into a root-only environment file read by systemd; an agent-readable copy (root:agent 0440 in a root:agent 0750 directory); exported by SFTP as agent into the per-instance directory on the host. Records carry fingerprints only.
credentials.scope: Every key-gated route of the outer Agent Server (profiles/strong-windows-qemu-whpx/agent-server/routes.json): one key, no per-route scope; it also mints the workspace and app-backend sessions.
credentials.lifetime: From provisioning until destroy; unchanged by a guest restart; new on recreate.
credentials.notes: Planned holder: management-dispatcher alone (E-01.2.x). Rotation today is recreate and provision only. The unit's ExecStartPre refuses to start the server without a valid key, because 1.60.1 serves an unsecured API when its key list is empty (S-01.3.1).

credentials.name: Agent Server OH_SECRET_KEY
credentials.storage: Root-only environment file in the guest (root:root 0600); never leaves the guest; searched for on the host by fingerprint only.
credentials.scope: Encryption of the server's stored secrets and runtime-control key material.
credentials.lifetime: From provisioning until destroy.

credentials.name: Per-conversation OH_SECRET_KEY and session key
credentials.storage: Passed by the Docker runtime as environment values into the conversation container; visible to anyone with Docker access (openhands and root); facts reports carry names only.
credentials.scope: That conversation's own inner Agent Server.
credentials.lifetime: The conversation container.

credentials.name: Membership of the guest's docker group
credentials.storage: Group membership: /run/docker.sock is root:docker 0660; containerd's socket is root:root 0660; no Moby TCP listener.
credentials.scope: The guest's Docker Engine API, which is root-equivalent inside the guest.
credentials.lifetime: The provisioned guest.

credentials.name: The Owner's Gitea account
credentials.storage: The non-administrator Gitea account aieh-owner. Owner directive of 2026-11-07: the Owner never signs in to Gitea or opens Credential Manager. Its final password was generated and set by task gitea:finalize-credentials on 2026-11-07 through Gitea's own forced change and is held in the credential provider entry "AIEH Gitea owner"; the temporary entry is deleted and the account holds no token. Its custodian is the authorization recorder (P-04.2; decision 0012, Proposed), which alone reads it, by name, into memory for each command, to merge as aieh-owner on a recorded Owner decision; it refuses an entry that names another account or holds a token. It is not read by agents, bots or tests (the recorder's tests use a fixture provider). Never an Owner PAT or session inside agent workspaces or CI runners.
credentials.scope: Merge allowlist of the protected authorization branch; review of exact operation manifests.
credentials.lifetime: Harness-held; rotated by rerunning credential finalization under the Owner's approval of 2026-11-07; no fixed lifetime yet.

credentials.name: Gitea site-administrator credential
credentials.storage: The Gitea site-administrator account aieh-site-admin. Owner directive of 2026-11-07: the Owner never signs in to Gitea or opens Credential Manager. Its final password was generated and set by task gitea:finalize-credentials on 2026-11-07 through Gitea's own forced change and is held in the credential provider entry "AIEH Gitea site-admin" (Windows: Credential Manager); the temporary entry is deleted, the temporary password no longer authenticates, and no password was found in the managed root, the checkout or the output. The same run revoked the account's three leftover tokens: S-01.2.2's unrevoked fixture token and two remediation probes (remediated exposure; a fixture-named probe answered 401 afterwards). Read only by credential finalization and the fixture administration; never exposed to agents, bots, tests or CI.
credentials.scope: Site administration, protection rules, impersonation.
credentials.lifetime: Harness-held; rotated by rerunning credential finalization under the Owner's approval of 2026-11-07; no fixed lifetime yet.

credentials.name: Engineering agent's Gitea bot token
credentials.storage: Bootstrap (S-01.2.2): one generic Windows Credential Manager entry of the Owner's account, "AIEH Gitea bot builder", written with CredWriteW from the Gitea CLI's captured output; records carry fingerprints only. Planned: delivered per attempt into the attempt environment only.
credentials.scope: Non-admin repository write and PR on the proposal branch; no merge, admin, protection, credential or executor privilege. Token scope write:repository only (Gitea 28.3.0 scopes are categorical; the repository and branch limits come from collaborator permission and branch protection)
credentials.lifetime: Gitea 28.3.0 has no token lifetime, so it is rotated at attempt end (planned). It is revoked by DELETE /api/v1/token, after which Gitea refuses it (observed, S-01.2.2).

credentials.name: Planning agent's Gitea bot token
credentials.storage: Bootstrap (S-01.2.2): one generic Windows Credential Manager entry of the Owner's account, "AIEH Gitea bot planner", written with CredWriteW from the Gitea CLI's captured output; records carry fingerprints only. Planned: delivered per attempt into the attempt environment only.
credentials.scope: Read the repositories in scope, push work/* proposal branches and open PRs whose writes are planning artefacts only (path-level realization pending the planning-artefact layout); no merge, protected-ref push, admin, protection, Work-status, executor, session-key or Docker privilege. Token scope write:repository only (Gitea 28.3.0 scopes are categorical; the repository and branch limits come from collaborator permission and branch protection)
credentials.lifetime: Gitea 28.3.0 has no token lifetime, so it is rotated at attempt end (planned). It is revoked by DELETE /api/v1/token, after which Gitea refuses it (observed, S-01.2.2).

credentials.name: Reviewer agent's Gitea bot token
credentials.storage: Bootstrap (S-01.2.2): one generic Windows Credential Manager entry of the Owner's account, "AIEH Gitea bot reviewer", written with CredWriteW from the Gitea CLI's captured output; records carry fingerprints only. Planned: delivered per attempt into the attempt environment only.
credentials.scope: Read the PR and submit a review; no merge, push to protected refs, admin or executor privilege. Token scope write:repository only (Gitea 28.3.0 scopes are categorical; the repository and branch limits come from collaborator permission and branch protection)
credentials.lifetime: Gitea 28.3.0 has no token lifetime, so it is rotated at attempt end (planned). It is revoked by DELETE /api/v1/token, after which Gitea refuses it (observed, S-01.2.2).

credentials.name: CI reporter's Gitea bot token (aieh-bot-ci)
credentials.storage: Planned: the dispatcher's custody on the host, as the other bot tokens; never in the CI guest or a job; records carry fingerprints only.
credentials.scope: Write collaborator of the governance repository and of each integration repository, whose ** protection denies it every push: triggers the governance workflow's workflow_dispatch (write on Actions) and posts aieh/validation on the proposal SHA (write on Code). Token scope write:repository only.
credentials.lifetime: Gitea 28.3.0 has no token lifetime; rotated by gitea_roles.py rotate as the other bot tokens.

credentials.name: CI job token (GITEA_TOKEN)
credentials.storage: Minted by Gitea per task (40 hex characters, salted hash); delivered to the runner as GITHUB_TOKEN and GITEA_TOKEN and placed by the runner in the job environment. It authenticates as the Actions pseudo-user bound to the task.
credentials.scope: Effective permission: none on every unit of the governance repository (restricted mode, all-none ceiling at owner and repository, permissions: {}); none on every other private repository (no AllowedCrossRepoIDs, no CollaborativeOwnerIDs); read on every public repository of the instance (irreducible; none exists by policy); accepted as a Bearer fallback by the v3 artifact route for its own task. Reach from the validation job: none (no network path). Relied on: never (decision 0016 (Proposed), section 5.3).
credentials.lifetime: One task: valid while the task is running or cancelling.

credentials.name: CI runtime token (gitea_runtime_token; expected as ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN)
credentials.storage: A JWT Gitea mints per task in the task context (HS256 with the instance's general token signing secret). Whether act_runner places it in the job environment is verified at Q-02.2.1; the lane treats it as present either way. Never recorded.
credentials.scope: Actions.Results:<run>:<job> plus cache write: accepted by the v3 and v4 artifact routes and by act_runner's cache server. Inert: no network path, the artifact routes denied by the filtering proxy, the cache server disabled. Relied on: never.
credentials.lifetime: One task; the JWT is valid from issue for 1 h plus ENDLESS_TASK_TIMEOUT (4 h at the default).

credentials.name: CI runner registration token
credentials.storage: The active row for the governance repository's scope in Gitea's database: it stays active after a registration until reset (Gitea 28.3.0). Never a file, a record, a log or the Owner's credential store. The host-side Gitea-administration command resets and reads it; the dispatcher carries it in memory once to the CI guest's register step; it is reset again after registration (decision 0016 (Proposed), section 6.3).
credentials.scope: Register a runner for the governance repository only.
credentials.lifetime: From reset to reset: minutes per provisioning.

credentials.name: CI runner token
credentials.storage: The runner's persistent token, issued by Gitea at registration (salted hash in Gitea's database); root-owned on the CI guest, outside every mount; never in a job.
credentials.scope: Poll and report the governance repository's tasks over the runner RPC (FetchTask, UpdateTask, UpdateLog) through the ci-control forward.
credentials.lifetime: Until the runner record is deleted (always at CI-guest destroy); for an ephemeral runner, until its single task ends.

credentials.name: Authorization verifier's read-only Gitea credential
credentials.storage: Bootstrap (S-01.2.2): one generic Windows Credential Manager entry of the Owner's account, "AIEH Gitea bot verifier", written with CredWriteW from the Gitea CLI's captured output; records carry fingerprints only. Planned: delivered per attempt into the attempt environment only. Unreachable from code runners.
credentials.scope: Read the protected authorization ref, PRs, merged_by and blobs. Token scope read:repository only.
credentials.lifetime: Gitea 28.3.0 has no token lifetime, so it is rotated at attempt end (planned). It is revoked by DELETE /api/v1/token, after which Gitea refuses it (observed, S-01.2.2).

credentials.name: Executor service identity
credentials.storage: A Windows service identity (a virtual service account preferred) with no stored password; never in the Owner's Credential Manager, never runas /savecred, never given to an agent.
credentials.scope: Modify on the effects root; allowlisted effect kinds only.
credentials.lifetime: Until the Owner revokes it.

credentials.name: Executor target credentials
credentials.storage: Separately credentialed, encrypted; unreachable from agents, CI and the Integration Service.
credentials.scope: The targets of allowlisted operation kinds; not defined until G-04.2.x.
credentials.lifetime: Not defined yet.

credentials.name: Brokered model-provider credential
credentials.storage: Host side, behind the brokered `inference` endpoint; never in the guest, the seed, a container or an agent-readable file.
credentials.scope: Model inference for engineering conversations.
credentials.lifetime: Not defined yet.

credentials.name: The Owner's UI session credential to the Owner host and Integration process
credentials.storage: Not defined: a separate Owner session credential, not shaped like an Agent Server key (decision 0013, point 5). Never in an agent workspace, CI runner, record, log or repository.
credentials.scope: The Owner UI's session to the Owner-host/Integration process on host loopback.
credentials.lifetime: The Owner's session (not defined further).
credentials.notes: No plan leaf names the Integration process's Owner login or this credential (plan silence, carried to U-01.2 and P-04.2).

credentials.name: A conversation's runtime credential, held by the Owner UI for that session
credentials.storage: Not stored: issued per Owner session by the dispatcher from the outer server's runtime-credentials route (POST /api/conversations/{id}/runtime/credentials, key-gated) and held only in the Owner UI's session; never in a record, log or repository (decision 0013, point 2). The conversation's agent can already read the conversation-bounded credential in its own container.
credentials.scope: That one conversation's inner server, over a dispatcher-owned local forward bound to host 127.0.0.1 (decision 0013, point 3); never the management API.
credentials.lifetime: The Owner's session, and no longer than the conversation's container.
credentials.notes: The response shape of the runtime-credentials route and Canvas 1.36.0's registration of a conversation are verified at U-01.2. Every forward it rides is a new host port and needs a recorded Owner approval (op-guest-boundary-change).

assets.name: The Owner's Windows host
assets.location: The trusted Owner host: Windows 11 Home, WHPX enabled (A1), the pinned QEMU (A2).

assets.name: The Owner's host credential stores
assets.location: The Owner's credential stores (protected for this leaf; not listed or read).

assets.name: Guest-state root
assets.location: The directory the Owner designated by act A3, outside the checkout and the Owner profile; ACL: the Owner's account, SYSTEM, Administrators. It holds the images, the pinned provider, the provision stage and the instances.

assets.name: Per-instance directory
assets.location: One directory per guest under the guest-state root: disks, seed, launch record, serial log, the SSH key and known_hosts, the exported session key, exchange staging. destroy removes it.

assets.name: QEMU process
assets.location: An ordinary user process of the Owner's account: no service, no elevation. The strong tier buys a kernel boundary, not a principal boundary.

assets.name: Host loopback SSH forward
assets.location: Host 127.0.0.1:{ssh_port} to guest :22 (hostfwd); classes management and exchange. Reachable by any local process; authentication by the per-instance key.

assets.name: QMP monitor
assets.location: Host 127.0.0.1:{qmp_port}, loopback TCP chardev, unauthenticated; host-only (refused from the guest). Full VM control.

assets.name: Strong execution guest
assets.location: Debian 13 under QEMU/WHPX (profile strong-windows-qemu-whpx): SLIRP restrict=on, ipv6=off, no host share, no guestfwd. The strong tier is not operational until S-02.x passes (C6).

assets.name: Repository exchange
assets.location: The guest's exchange directory and its host staging: git bundles only, bounded in size; pull never writes into the Owner's repositories.

assets.name: Guest sshd
assets.location: Base-image sshd on 0.0.0.0:22 and [::]:22 in the guest; root login refused. Unreachable from the container bridges: the container guard refuses every new connection from docker0 or br-* to the guest (S-01.3.1).

assets.name: Outer Agent Server listener
assets.location: The guest's 127.0.0.1:8000 only (explicit --host 127.0.0.1); class management, guest-local; not forwarded to the host (the Agent Server host forward is deferred).

assets.name: Conversation container listeners
assets.location: One docker-proxy listener per running owned container on the guest's 127.0.0.1 at an ephemeral port, mapped to the container's port 8000; never forwarded to the host.

assets.name: Guest Docker daemon socket
assets.location: /run/docker.sock, root:docker 0660; agent gets EACCES; never mounted into a conversation container. Absent from every job: the path does not exist inside a conversation container (ENOENT, S-01.3.2).

assets.name: Guest containerd socket
assets.location: /run/containerd/containerd.sock, root:root 0660; the CRI plugin is off, so no streaming listener. Absent from every job: neither it nor its .ttrpc companion exists inside a conversation container (ENOENT, S-01.3.2).

assets.name: Agent Server secrets environment file
assets.location: /etc/aieh/agent-server/secrets.env, root:root 0600; agent gets EACCES.

assets.name: Agent-readable session key file
assets.location: /var/lib/aieh/agent-server/session.key, root:agent 0440, in a root:agent 0750 directory.

assets.name: Single-use root provisioning step
assets.location: aieh-provision.path and .service, seeded by cloud-init: triggered once by a host marker; copies, verifies against seed-pinned sha256 values, installs with native tools, deletes the upload and disables itself.

assets.name: Root read-only facts reporters
assets.location: aieh-docker-facts (every boot) and aieh-conversation-facts (on demand: agent creates a request file in a root:agent 0730 directory; the reporter removes it unread, runs docker ps and container inspect only, redacts secret values; at most 20 runs in 60 s, then fails closed until the next boot).

assets.name: Container guard, egress guard and key check (management API admission, container egress)
assets.location: aieh-container-guard.service (seeded; docker.service Requires and starts After it): an INPUT chain for IPv4 and IPv6 that logs (rate-limited, kernel log) and refuses every new connection from docker0 or br-* to the guest itself, TCP with a reset; icc false in daemon.json; and the Agent Server unit's ExecStartPre key check, which refuses to start the server without a valid session key. Verified by the root step's admission step, reported by the boot facts and checked by inspect. S-01.4: the same script and unit also install the egress guard: Moby's DOCKER-USER chain (created by the guard when absent) sends every new forwarded connection from docker0 or br-* to another interface to AIEH-EGRESS-GUARD, which logs (rate-limited, prefix aieh-egress-guard: ) and refuses it, TCP with a reset, IPv4 and IPv6, with an empty allowlist. Observed on a fresh guest: the rules survived Moby's first start and a guest restart unchanged; SLIRP's 10.0.2.2 and 10.0.2.3 and an unconfigured guestfwd-class address were refused from both jobs with the guard's counters rising by exactly the refused attempts; off-link addresses are answered by the guest's routing before the guard (no default route). Fix-forward (the Overseer's ruling): with a temporary default route via 10.0.2.2 in a falsification guest (create --provision --egress-falsification), 1.1.1.1:443 and 8.8.8.8:53, TCP and UDP, were refused from both jobs by the egress guard (counters +4 tcp-reset and +2 REJECT, exactly the attempts; log OUT=enp0s4), before and after a restart; the route was removed and verified gone each time. The guard, not the missing route, holds off-link egress.

assets.name: Conversation container
assets.location: One per Docker conversation: the locked image ID, three binds under the server's scratch, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, the server's uid:gid, Moby's default bridge with host.docker.internal mapped to the guest's docker0. Its inner server also starts VSCode on port 8001 inside its network namespace. icc is off on the default bridge (no connection between containers), and the container guard refuses its new connections to any address of the guest (S-01.3.1). It is the job environment of builder and reviewer runs (S-01.3.2, declared in provisioning.agent_server.jobs): not privileged, no added capability, device or host namespace, SecurityOpt exactly no-new-privileges with Moby's builtin seccomp profile and AppArmor docker-default; inside it uid 999 gid 989 with no supplementary group, every capability set empty, NoNewPrivs 1, Seccomp 2. No engine socket exists in it (every Docker, containerd, Podman, BuildKit and CRI-O path ENOENT; no socket file, no bound unix name), the engine ports 2375 and 2376 refuse at every address it can see, and no management, Owner, admin or bot credential is in its files or process environments (searched by fingerprint). The image ships docker, ctr, containerd and runc binaries and setuid-root sudo and su, inert there (fd-job-image-engine-clients). Since S-01.4 the egress guard refuses its new connections out of the guest (SLIRP's aliases, unconfigured guestfwd addresses); off-link addresses have no route in the guest.

assets.name: Outer Agent Server management API
assets.location: /api/* (and /v1/*, /app-backends/*, /sockets/*) on the guest's 127.0.0.1:8000. Every route of 1.60.1 is listed in profiles/strong-windows-qemu-whpx/agent-server/routes.json (193: 10 public reads, 12 management reads, 171 privileged) with its credential and expected refusal. Without the session key or with a wrong one every key-gated HTTP route answers 401, a WebSocket is closed with 4001 or its handshake refused (403), and the Canvas App backend proxy answers 503 (ingress not configured) (S-01.3.1, all 193 probed live). The listener is unreachable from the conversation containers at every guest address. The trusted dispatcher's lifecycle and inspection routes are marked allowed in the inventory; the server cannot scope its key per route.

assets.name: Outer Agent Server unauthenticated routes
assets.location: /server_info, /alive and /openapi.json answered without the key on the guest loopback; read only.

assets.name: Agent Server capability routes beyond the conversation lifecycle
assets.location: The routes behind the capability families /server_info advertises at 1.60.1, enumerated in profiles/strong-windows-qemu-whpx/agent-server/routes.json: credential bindings, settings and secrets, agent profiles, meta-profiles, profiles, skills, plugins, LLM models, provider connections and subscriptions, MCP, Canvas extensions and app backends, workspaces, files, git, bash, hooks, sub-agents, ACP, the OpenAI-compatible /v1 routes, VSCode, POST /api/init, the auth workspace session, the WebSockets and the Docker runtime's conversation proxy. Each needs the session key or a credential the key mints (S-01.3.1). The usable tool start_child_conversation sends its request to the conversation's own inner server, not to this API.

assets.name: Guest Docker Engine API
assets.location: Over /run/docker.sock only; reached by the server's docker CLI as openhands. Not reachable from a job: no socket inside a conversation container, and no TCP endpoint (2375 and 2376 refuse at host.docker.internal, every guest address, the container's own loopback and SLIRP's 10.0.2.2 and 10.0.2.3; the peer container does not answer) (S-01.3.2).

It holds no credential and connects to no backend yet; it is the Owner UI of decision 0013, in td-owner.

assets.name: Gitea server
assets.location: Gitea 28.3.0, the pinned Windows binary (composition/lock/components.lock.json), as a host-loopback service: HTTP on 127.0.0.1:13300 only, plus Gitea's built-in egress-policy proxy on a kernel-assigned 127.0.0.1 port. It runs as the Owner's Windows account without elevation, inside a supervisor's kill-on-close Job Object (integrations/gitea/gitea_host.py). Its binary is an asset in the managed data root's assets/release-binaries/gitea/28.3.0/, its configuration and SQLite state are in persistent/gitea/ and its logs in persistent/logs/gitea/ (default root %LOCALAPPDATA%\AIEH). Sign-in is required, registration is disabled, there is no SSH server, and it runs offline.

findings.title: Host-side bootstrap agents share the Owner's Windows account
findings.detail: The host-side agent sessions run as the Owner's account and are not independently isolated security principals. Every credential and store in that account's custody (the public-repository push credential, the provider login, the guest SSH keys, the exported session keys, QMP, the guest-state root, the integration store) is reachable by them. Their elevation is gated by the Owner's interactive UAC consent, which is not an OS security boundary. This is the accepted bootstrap limit; the guest boundary is the boundary against untrusted agents, and the genuine OS boundary for privileged effects is the executor's separate identity (G-04.2.1). No credential is designated to an agent principal here; the reachability is disclosed, not prevented. Since F-06.1 this includes the host-loopback Gitea: any process of the Owner's account, host agents included, can read Gitea's app.ini secrets (SECRET_KEY, INTERNAL_TOKEN, JWT_SECRET) and its SQLite database under the managed data root. The INTERNAL_TOKEN reaches Gitea's private API, and write access to the database can change any account, its administrator flag or its password hash, so such a process can forge or take over Gitea sessions and identities, the site administrator's and the Owner account's included. The two temporary passwords in Credential Manager, and after task gitea:finalize-credentials the two harness-held final passwords, are readable the same way. The final passwords exist only as Gitea's password hashes. Directory placement is not a security boundary (decision 0009, point 11). Since S-01.2.2 it also includes the four bot tokens in Credential Manager ("AIEH Gitea bot <role>"), which CredReadW returns to any process of the account without a prompt, and Gitea's CLI, which mints a token for any account, the site administrator's and the Owner account's included, without a password. None of this is reachable from the execution guest (profiles P3-P5, F-03.3.1).

findings.title: Owner authorization is a recorded decision, not an authenticated one
findings.detail: Narrowed at P-04.2, not closed. An Owner authorization is now a recorded decision: the authorization recorder (decision 0012, Proposed) records the Owner's statement in the shared Owner decision record (kind authorize-operation), binds it to the exact head and manifest digest of the proposal, writes a write-ahead receipt to the integration store and merges as aieh-owner with the decision's trailers; merged_by aieh-owner means merged under Owner authority by the recorder, never by the Owner. What remains: in the bootstrap channel the statement is the Owner's verbatim reply in the main-session conversation, transcribed by the Overseer, which proves a declared decision bound to an exact revision, not an authenticated Owner (the target channel is an authenticated Owner host session); aieh-owner cannot read the branch protection rule in Gitea 28.3.0 (repository or site administrators only), so the other accounts on the allowlists and the override flags are not compared before a merge; processes of the Owner's account can reach the credential (decision 0010); no authorization repository, verifier or Owner authorization exists yet, and the recorder has run against a fake Gitea only. During bootstrap the Owner's other decisions still reach the repository as records the Overseer writes (decisions/, evidence/bootstrap-log.md).

findings.title: The operator login `agent` reads the management key; no agent workload has that login
findings.detail: Custody as of S-01.3.1. No dispatcher exists. During bootstrap the dispatcher's role is performed by the Owner's account through tools/guest.py, over the instance's host-loopback SSH forward with the per-instance key, as the operator login agent, which reads the session key from its root:agent 0440 file inside the guest (never on a command line). No agent workload ever has that login: an engineering agent runs in a conversation container as 999:989 in its own namespaces, holds no SSH key, cannot reach the guest's sshd (the container guard refuses it at every guest address), cannot reach the management listener, and its readable process environments hold only its own conversation keys (the outer key's fingerprint was absent from both containers, S-01.3.1). The name still collides with the engineering-agent role, and anyone given the login would hold the full management key. Moving the key to a separate guest identity (a dispatch group that agent is not in) is proposed to the Overseer, not done; whether the login keeps the key once a dispatcher exists is decided with the dispatcher (E-01.2.x). S-01.3.2: no job holds the login, its SSH key or the management key: the outer key's fingerprints are absent from every readable file and process environment of two conversation containers, and sshd, the management listener and the instance's host forwards refuse from them. Custody beyond bootstrap stays with E-01.2.2. S-01.4 (ruling R9): the session-key file stays where it is; the finding is carried to E-01.2.2 and E-01.3.1.

findings.title: One session key grants the whole management API
findings.detail: The outer Agent Server accepts one X-Session-API-Key for every key-gated route; there is no per-route or per-role scope, and the only rotation is recreate and provision. S-01.3.1 enumerated the routes (193; the key admits 166 HTTP routes directly and mints the workspace and app-backend sessions) and marks in the route inventory which ones the trusted dispatcher may call: that allowlist is the dispatcher's policy, not a server control. What the server and the guest enforce is admission by key and by network: the listener is on the guest's loopback only, the unit drops non-loopback packets, and the container guard refuses every new connection from a container bridge to the guest. The blueprint warns not to assume a session API key is a fine-grained permission token. S-01.4 narrows its reach without changing the mechanism: by decision 0013 no browser, UI process, Integration process or agent ever holds the key; the Owner UI reaches a session only with that conversation's runtime credential.

findings.title: start_child_conversation reaches only the conversation's own inner server
findings.detail: Established at S-01.3.1 from the locked binary and live: the tool (openhands-tools child_conversation) posts to OH_INTERNAL_SERVER_URL + /api/conversations/{parent}/children with the key of the agent-server running it. In a conversation container that URL is http://127.0.0.1:8000, the inner server, and the key is the conversation's own (cred-conversation-keys); the inner server is a local runtime (OH_CONVERSATION_RUNTIME=local), so a child runs in the same container. From inside both disposable containers the inner children route answered 401 without a key and 422 with the inner key and an empty body (nothing created); the outer listener refused the inner key at every address (no connection); the outer count stayed 2. The tool therefore cannot invoke privileged conversation creation on the outer server. Not exercised: a valid child launch, which would start an agent step and an LLM call. A child in the same container shares that container's caps and mounts: E-01.2.2's ceilings.

findings.title: Conversation containers keep upstream network defaults
findings.detail: Recorded deviations: --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway (the guest's docker0), Moby's default bridge instead of --network none, and create-request caps that replace the server's without an upper bound. Observed at S-01.3.1 before the admission controls: from a conversation container the guest's sshd (172.17.0.1:22 and 10.0.2.15:22, banner) and systemd-resolved's LLMNR (TCP 5355) were reachable, and the other container's inner server (8000, /server_info 200) and VSCode (8001, 403) too; the management listener and the published ports refused. After them (container guard, icc false): every guest address and port refuses (TCP reset, logged) and the peer container times out, in both containers and after a guest restart. Remaining: host.docker.internal still names the guest (refused), the container keeps a NAT path out through the guest (no route out, SLIRP restrict=on; the deny-by-default matrix is S-01.4), and the request caps override (E-01.2.2). S-01.3.2: the locked server adds host.docker.internal unconditionally and its Config has no option to remove it (Moby's host-gateway-ip would retarget, not remove, the name), so the mapping stays, refused at every port. Through the NAT path, SLIRP's 10.0.2.2 (the host's loopback: the SSH forward, QMP and the host Gitea's 13300) and 10.0.2.3 refuse every probed port; the deny-by-default matrix stays with S-01.4. S-01.4: the NAT path out through the guest is closed by policy: the egress guard in Moby's DOCKER-USER chain (provisioning.agent_server.admission.network.egress_guard, empty allowlist; S-03.x adds the first entry for inference) refuses every new forwarded connection from a container bridge to another interface, logged, TCP with a reset; off-link addresses have no route in the guest (topology, beside the policy). Remaining, recorded limits: host.docker.internal still names the guest (refused at every port by the container guard), the request caps that override the server's (E-01.2.2), and the absence of --network none, re-tested by S-02.1 and S-02.2. Observed at S-01.4 on a fresh guest, before and after a restart: from both jobs, TCP to 10.0.2.2 (the SSH forward, QMP, 13300) and 10.0.2.3:53, UDP to 10.0.2.3:53 and TCP to 10.0.2.100:7000 were refused by the egress guard (counters +10 tcp-reset and +2 REJECT, exactly the refused attempts; logged); 1.1.1.1:443 and 8.8.8.8:53 got ENETUNREACH and UDP 8.8.8.8:53 a timeout from the guest's routing, so the guard does not engage for off-link destinations: under the dispatch's fixed decision rule that part is a FAIL (topology, not policy), recorded, with no connection. Fix-forward (the Overseer's ruling): with a temporary default route via 10.0.2.2 in a falsification guest (create --provision --egress-falsification), 1.1.1.1:443 and 8.8.8.8:53, TCP and UDP, were refused from both jobs by the egress guard (counters +4 tcp-reset and +2 REJECT, exactly the attempts; log OUT=enp0s4), before and after a restart; the route was removed and verified gone each time. The guard, not the missing route, holds off-link egress. S-02.1 re-tested the absence of --network none as a recorded deviation (each job has eth0 on Moby's default bridge and lo) that passes only while its compensating cases pass: the egress guard refused SLIRP's aliases and the unconfigured guestfwd-class address, it refused the off-link targets with a route present (exact counters, OUT= the uplink), the peer's inner server timed out (icc) and the management listener and the engine ports refused (container guard); host.docker.internal:host-gateway likewise; in two runs around a guest restart.

findings.title: Conversation containers run as the Agent Server's service uid
findings.detail: The Docker runtime starts each container with --user of the server's uid:gid (openhands, 999:989), the principal that is in group docker. The separation of the untrusted workload from the server rests on the container's namespaces, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges and the absent socket mount, with no user-namespace remap. Each conversation's keys are environment values visible to openhands and root through docker inspect. S-01.3.2 narrowed it: the container gets the uid and primary gid only (no supplementary group, so not docker), every capability set is empty, no_new_privs and seccomp are set, and no engine socket or engine endpoint exists in it. A user-namespace remap or another runtime would be a structural change (not made; an architecture question for S-02.1). S-02.1 narrowed it further (the containment probes, two runs on one fresh guest around a restart; probe validation, not the S-02.2 acceptance run): through every mount a job has, uid 999 can write only its own three binds (its workspace, its runtime home and its own conversation store); the only other disk-backed mounts are Moby's resolv.conf, hostname and hosts, which it cannot write; no other conversation's workspace or store is reachable (ENOENT by the guest path, by the bind-mount source and through /proc/*/root; no disk-backed mount is shared between two jobs), and no process of another uid is visible. Remaining: the job can write its own conversation's stored state, which the outer server persists and reads (base_state.json, meta.json, bash_events, the owner lease); whether a tampered file can steer the outer server is not tested. A user-namespace remap or another runtime stays a structural question that no observation here calls for. S-02.2's acceptance run (111/111 PASS before and after a guest restart) re-observed the narrowed reach and did not test the residual. By the Owner's ruling of 2026-11-07 the stored-state question stays untested and open, and is carried to E-01.2.2 together with an observed drill that a missing guard or key blocks activation (so far declared in S-01.3.1, S-01.3.2 and S-01.4). E-01.2.2 answered the residual: a tampered file can steer the outer server. Slice (b) altered every field of the job-writable stored state alone (136): base_state.json execution_status running makes the pinned 1.60.1 outer server resume the conversation in its own process at its next start, and with a stored working directory it creates that host path; the job can persist running itself (fd-outer-server-local-recovery). Compensating control (slice (c)): a seeded root quiesce step runs before every server start, removes every container, rewrites a stored running record to error and moves aside a record that is a link, a hard link, of another owner or of another conversation's id; the server Requires it and Moby. Re-observed live on fresh guests in slice (c), with the F-2 closed drill (evidence/E-01.2.2c-fix-requalification.md). What a job can still write is its own record as the catalog and UI show it (status words, title, the working_dir text, a self-inflicted 404 or 500), and the execution_status that the outer server reports while the conversation runs is the job's own value: E-01.5 takes its executing signal from the container's existence (root facts), never from that stored status (Overseer ruling R2).

findings.title: The pinned Agent Server resumes job-written stored conversations in its own process at start
findings.detail: A recorded limit of the pinned OpenHands Agent Server 1.60.1 in Docker runtime mode (finding F-2 of E-01.2.2 slice (b)). At every start ConversationService.__aenter__ loads the catalog from conversations_path, which is also each conversation container's own writable bind, and hydrates every record whose base_state.json says running as a local conversation in the outer process: it imports the stored tool_module_qualnames and registers stored client tools and agent definitions before it claims the conversation's lease, then claims the lease, creates the stored workspace.working_dir and runs git init there (EventService.start at v1.60.1); in Docker mode the claim succeeds because the runtime cleanup at start has already removed every conversation container, so no inner server holds the lease (evidence/OA-03-openhands-resume-report.md section 1.2 item 5); no configuration turns it off, and catalog records are keyed by the stored meta.json id, not the directory name. The outer process is the management principal (openhands, group docker). Loading job-supplied code was not established (no job-writable path is on the import path; the frozen binary's sys.path was not inspected). Compensating control: the seeded root quiesce step before every server start (profile provisioning.agent_server.quiesce; slice (c)), which removes every container first and leaves no stored running record, and quarantines a record of another conversation's id or a link. Residuals: meta.json is parsed by the step with the standard library and by the server with pydantic, so a meta.json that only the server's parser accepts escapes the id check (inference, not tested); the step trusts the root-owned configuration for the conversations path. Upstream report to be filed against 1.60.1 (skip local recovery for Docker-backed conversations, or confine it to the status repair; a lease check alone would not help in Docker mode, where the start-up cleanup leaves the lease free); carried to decision 0001's version line: when a pinned release carries the fix, keeping or retiring the step is a recorded decision.

findings.title: The conversation image ships engine clients and setuid-root helpers
findings.detail: The locked agent-server image holds docker, ctr, containerd and runc binaries and setuid-root sudo, su, mount and passwd, and its own openhands user (uid 10001) is in group sudo. In a job they are inert: no engine socket or engine TCP endpoint exists or answers, the container runs as 999:989 with no passwd entry, no_new_privs makes the kernel ignore setuid (sudo refuses), su needs a password and every capability set is empty (S-01.3.2). Each control is independent of the others, but a job that gained an engine endpoint would find the client already installed. The image is upstream's and pinned by ID (decision 0006 item 3). S-02.1 ran the clients in two jobs, twice: docker version (Docker CLI 29.9.3) and ctr version (v2.4.2) exit non-zero with no engine endpoint (no socket); sudo -n true and su refuse (no_new_privs; a password); a raw socket, a user or mount namespace, a device node and a module load are refused with EPERM (no capability; Moby's seccomp filters unshare for every flag value).

findings.title: Host loopback control surfaces are open to every local process
findings.detail: QMP is an unauthenticated loopback TCP socket with full VM control, and the SSH forward is a loopback port protected by the per-instance key. Both are reachable by any local process of any user on the host: disclosed, not prevented (the standard library has no AF_UNIX on Windows). S-01.4 (decision 0013, point 6): same-account host processes are outside the threat model on the host network plane too (blueprint #security and #containment-architecture, read with decision 0010, point 1; 0010 is not amended), so this exposure is a disclosed limit. What is enforced is that every harness host listener binds 127.0.0.1 only (the LAN reaches none of them; guest.py host-census), and that the guest reaches neither listener (SLIRP restrict=on).

findings.title: No accepted record names the release-signing and deployment principal
findings.detail: The blueprint reserves persistent release credentials for 'separate, narrowly authorized jobs' in 'a separately credentialed environment', and also lists the runner and the privileged executor among the build and deploy tools. No accepted record says whether release signing and deployment run as the privileged executor, as a dedicated trusted runner, or as something else. The inventory names the role only as an unknown placeholder principal and does not decide it. S-01.2.1 narrows it without deciding it (decision 0007, Proposed): the principal is on the trusted side only, never ci-job or any agent role; its credential is of a privileged class; activation goes through op-effect-apply; and the signing identity is distinct from the executor's effect identity unless Q-02.4 decides otherwise. Q-02.4 and G-04.2.1 decide it.

findings.title: No CI runner is selected or pinned
findings.detail: composition/ pins Gitea but no runner. The runner's class is decided by decision 0016 (Proposed; policy/ci-runner-profile.json): act_runner in a dedicated disposable CI guest, its only path off the guest the ci-control forward to Gitea's runner RPC (an Owner act); the validation job reaches nothing, and its two task tokens are inert and permissionless (decision 0013, point 7, unchanged). Still open: the pinned runner binary and job image, the CI profile variant, the P7 ci-control class and the matrix edits (Q-02.2.1), and the act_runner facts the profile relies on (A1 of policy/ci-token-secret-policy.json).

findings.title: A read-permission collaborator can open a pull request in Gitea 28.3.0
findings.detail: Observed at S-01.2.2: the reviewer bot, a read collaborator of the fixture with a write:repository token (Gitea needs that scope to submit a review), opened a pull request from an existing branch (201); it could not open an issue (write:issue), push, merge or change settings. Gitea has no review-only permission, so the reviewer's 'read and review only' realization holds except for opening PRs. Opening a PR is not an Owner operation: merges stay with the merge allowlist.

findings.title: A Gitea job token reads every public repository, and a status context is forgeable by any writer on Code
findings.detail: At the pin (Q-02.1 step 1, source-level): the Actions user's individual read is added after every ceiling, so every job token reads every public repository of the instance; the lane's policy is that no public repository exists, and the live check reports any that does. Required status checks match contexts by glob, not creators, so any holder of write on Code can post aieh/validation; every such holder is a trusted-side custodian, and the promotion lane trusts the run record the verifier re-reads, not the status.

findings.title: Gitea bot and token behaviour is unverified at the pinned version
findings.detail: The blueprint's SEC-02 qualification cites Gitea 28 token-only bot accounts and audit logging and names 28.2.0 as its baseline; composition/ pins 28.3.0. Observed on the running 28.3.0 instance at S-01.2.2: the Bot account type (no password), the restricted flag (a public repository is invisible to a restricted account), categorical token scopes (read: and write: of activitypub, issue, misc, notification, organization, package, repository, user and admin, plus all), no token lifetime, self-revocation through DELETE /api/v1/token, the site administrator listing and revoking another account's token, sudo refused to non-administrators, the reverse-proxy user header ignored, reviews needing write:repository, and branch protection (push and merge allowlists, force-push and deletion denied, the administrator's merge override blocked). Still unverified: audit logging (off by default). Read at source in gitea-src-28.3.0 at Q-02.1, not live: the Actions facts G1 to G10 of policy/ci-token-secret-policy.json (the configurable token ceilings, the registration token active until reset, every owner and repository secret delivered to every task, the status contexts, the owner-only Actions secret, variable and runner routes, scoped workflows); live verification is Q-02.3.1's.

findings.title: The Owner UI reaches a session only with its conversation-bounded runtime credential
findings.detail: Decided by decision 0013 (Proposed at S-01.4): no browser, UI process, Integration process or agent ever holds the management key; the Owner UI reaches an engineering session only with that conversation's runtime credential (cred-conversation-runtime-access), issued per session by the dispatcher, over a dispatcher-owned local forward bound to host 127.0.0.1; its credential to the Owner-host/Integration process is a separate Owner session credential (cred-owner-ui-session). Both are planned: no forward, credential or registration exists (U-01.2, E-01.3.x; every forward is a new host port and needs a recorded Owner approval). Disclosed residual: the UI and the conversation's agent share that conversation-bounded credential, which the agent can already read in its own container, so a UI compromise is bounded to that attempt. Until S-01.4 the access was undefined (unknown).

findings.title: No plan leaf names the Integration process's Owner login or the UI session credential
findings.detail: Decision 0013 (point 5) makes the Owner UI's credential to the Owner-host/Integration process a separate Owner session credential, not shaped like an Agent Server key. No plan leaf names that login or builds the credential: U-01.1 built the shell with no backend and no credential, U-01.2 wires navigation to engineering detail, and P-04.2 builds the Owner authorization recorder. Recorded as plan silence (S-01.4 ruling R8), not settled here.

findings.title: Custody of the Owner's own credentials was not inspected
findings.detail: Credential stores are protected for this leaf, so the storage, scope and lifetime of the Owner's push credential and provider login are not established. Their existence is evident from the recorded pushes and headless runs.

findings.title: How an engineering agent's coding provider authenticates is not defined
findings.detail: The ACP provider's default session mode is bypassPermissions, so it cannot be the isolation boundary. Provider credentials may only sit behind the brokered inference endpoint, which is deferred; how the provider inside a conversation container authenticates without holding an Owner or long-lived credential is not yet specified. S-01.2.1 fixes that no provider credential is ever a role token: the inference broker alone issues per-attempt inference access. No plan leaf owns the broker (a plan gap routed to the Owner).
